title: Make the Stage Console theme fluent on the tablet
notes: Earlier runs showed the backend unlinked, so every tile was drawn disabled and the connection dot animated without pause; measure linked: start the mock master on the Mac (`tests/qt_mock_server.py` with the `vc-vibra.json` fixture on a fixed port) and run `/data/qt-full/taps/drive-mock.sh` with `BACKEND=/data/qt-full/backend-mock` (adds `--host <mac> --port <port>`). Linked on 2026-10-26: flat theme 18-22 ms p50 per frame, Stage Console 58 ms with ~145 draw batches. Grouping every tile's ring, fill and baked look into `TileGlassLayers` (so they batch) and baking live tiles' glass into `fill-*` looks brought it to 36 ms and 59 batches (flat: ~50). Frame intervals land on 60 Hz vsync multiples (18, 36, 51 ms), so the GPU is now just over one refresh: removing the backdrop gave 24 ms, and any single full-window layer costs ~12 ms whether a gradient Rectangle or an image. Runs vary by about 5 ms; compare variants over repeated runs. Tried without gain (36 ms, two runs each): caching the floor and panels in one `layer.enabled` texture, and opaque occluder rectangles inside panels and tiles (the GPU did not skip what they covered). Next: get under one refresh without losing the floor, e.g. draw the floor only where panels leave it visible, and confirm with repeated runs whether removing the floor really reaches one refresh. Later on 2026-10-26 the floor became one window-sized BMP (the ChatGPT floor plate) instead of two images and the live tiles took looks sliced from the ChatGPT tile sheet: linked runs gave 37 and then 36 ms medians, level with before, and no image warnings. On 2026-10-27 the cause of the ~12 ms per full-window layer was found: the Mali-400 runs at a fixed 148.5 MHz (`aclk_gpu` = gpll 594 MHz / 4, no devfreq), because taq102 v67 removed the GPU OPP table after a hang at 480 MHz (taq102 `TODO.md`, RK816 regulator item). The vendor table (`kernel/rk3126-taq102-hybrid.dts`, phandle 0x19) gives 300 MHz at 1.05 V, and the logic rails read 1.1 V, so a fixed `assigned-clock-rates` of 297 MHz (gpll_div2) on `&gpu` would stay in spec without regulator control and should roughly halve GPU time. It needs a taq102 boot image flashed to `boot` and `recovery`. Blocked: the owner decides on the firmware later (2026-10-27); do not flash or touch the venue machines until then. The C desk draws through dumb buffers, not the GPU, so a GPU hang would only stop the Qt trial. On 2026-11-02 the GPU was ruled out as the limit: raised at runtime from 148.5 to 297 MHz, the median frame moved from 35 to 38 ms. The tablet is CPU-bound, with one core at 600 MHz (`nosmp`; see taq102 `TODO.md`). A tab switch rebuilt every ControlTile, because a `Repeater` with an integer model recreates all its delegates when the count changes (41 tiles of about 45 items each), and every snapshot rebuilt each Repeater whose model was an array made in a binding (48 items per BPM tick). Tiles are now a pool that only grows and hides what a page does not use, and the Repeaters count instead of taking fresh arrays; `qt-desk-snapshot-reuse` guards both and fails against the previous QML (tick: 48 destroyed; without the pool: 41 tiles destroyed). On the tablet, two runs each of `taps/drive.sh` (55 s of tab switches): before, 41-44 frames, p90 frame 297-323 ms, p90 sync 180 ms; after, 111-118 frames, p90 frame 71-77 ms, p90 sync 42 ms. The median stays near 40 ms, mostly `swap`. Later the same night, a Mac bench feeding QVariantMap snapshots through the test bridge, as DeskBridge does (offscreen, software), showed that the shared pool still rebound every tile on a tab switch (bindings 20 ms of 29 ms). Each page now keeps its own tiles, and a tile takes a control only when its JSON differs, so a page round trip hands no tile a control again. Same session, against 19dfe70: tab switch 29-30 ms to 6.5-8.8 ms, snapshot about 12 ms to 5.7-6.6 ms. `qt-desk-snapshot-reuse` now also counts `modelData` reassignments: 123 on 19dfe70, 0 now. On the tablet, two runs each of `taps/drive.sh` (2026-11-02): 19dfe70 gave 112 frames, p90 frame 75-77 ms, p90 sync 42 ms; 5b3541a gave 113-115 frames, p90 frame 46-47 ms, p90 sync 10 ms. `/data/qt-full/qml` is now 5b3541a (previous kept as `qml.19dfe70`). The median frame stays at 36 ms, mostly `swap`. On 2026-11-03 taq102 brought all four cores up through PSCI (taq102 1fd4309): two drives of the same QML gave 124-125 frames, p90 frame 40-41 ms, p90 sync 5-6 ms, median 35 ms. Since taq102 v101 (2026-11-03) the Mali boots at 297 MHz. With QLC+ closed, measured against the Mac mock master (`tests/qt_mock_server.py` fixture on 192.168.1.87:9411, tablet wrapper `/data/qt-full/backend-mock-mini`, `taps/drive-mock.sh`), two runs each on v101: Mali 297 MHz median 27 ms, p90 35 ms, p90 sync 3-5 ms; the same image with the Mali set back to 148.5 MHz at runtime, median 35 ms, p90 39-40 ms. The mock closes the socket twice in the first ~10 s of each run, before the taps start, so frame counts (142-187) are not comparable; the medians are. Those closes were the mock's own 0.5 s idle timeout, fixed on 2026-11-04 (`qt-mock-idle`), so later runs keep one link. Also seen that day on the panel: right after link-up the colour and opacity motions take about 2 s to settle (connection dot still red 6 s after start, teal at 8 s), so the first linked frames are slow. Next: CPU frequency, still 600 MHz (taq102 `TODO.md`).
